title: Epigastric Pain

rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: Assess severity — may appear very ill.
rationale.Physical Exam: Abdomen: Epigastric tenderness + guarding. Grey Turner (flank) / Cullen (periumbilical) in severe hemorrhagic pancreatitis.
rationale.BMP / CMP / LFTs: Elevated AST/ALT/ALP/bilirubin if gallstone etiology. Elevated BUN ≥20 at 48h = poor prognosis.
rationale.Lipase: >3x ULN = diagnostic. More sensitive and specific than amylase.
rationale.RUQ ultrasound: Check for gallstones — most common cause.
rationale.CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast: At 48-72h if not improving. Assess for necrosis, pseudocyst, abscess.
rationale.IV fluids (Lactated Ringer preferred): Aggressive resuscitation. LR preferred over NS — reduces systemic inflammation. 250-500 mL/hr initially.
rationale.Diet, NPO: Initially NPO for bowel rest. Advance to clear liquids as pain improves.
rationale.IV analgesics (Morphine / Hydromorphone): Pain management. Morphine is acceptable — does NOT worsen pancreatitis (old teaching was incorrect).
rationale.Prophylactic antibiotics in all pancreat: Antibiotics NOT indicated for sterile pancreatic necrosis. Only for confirmed infected necrosis or concurrent infection. Prophylaxis does not improve outcomes.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and low-grade fever. Exam reveals epigastric tenderness with guarding, jaundiced sclera, and possibly Grey Turner/Cullen signs in severe cases. Most common causes: gallstones (GET SMASHED mnemonic — Gallstones, Ethanol, Trauma, Steroids, Mumps, Autoimmune, Scorpion stings, Hypercalcemia/Hypertriglyceridemia, ERCP, Drugs). Diagnosis requires 2 of 3: (1) characteristic epigastric pain, (2) lipase/amylase >3x upper limit, (3) CT findings. Lipase is more sensitive and specific than amylase (especially in delayed presentation). Ranson criteria and BISAP score for severity. Management: aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (LR preferred over NS), NPO initially, IV analgesics (morphine OK), antiemetics. Early enteral nutrition within 24-48h (NG or NJ feeds). ERCP within 24h if gallstone pancreatitis with cholangitis or obstruction. CT with contrast at 48-72h if not improving to assess for necrosis/complications.

Epigastric tenderness with guarding. Assess for Grey Turner (flank ecchymosis) and Cullen (periumbilical ecchymosis) — retroperitoneal hemorrhage.
